messages.author: 5914e579c97f1326
messages.subject: spatio-temporal areal level modelling
parts:
I am running a spatio-temporal model using areal level data for a number of outcome variables. The time points represent different years, however, the years are not regular over time ( eg i have 1989, 1994, 2000, 2003, 2005, 2006 etc). What's the minimum separation that's allowed  so that I can predictions for every year.  That is: are the years between 1994 and 2000 to many to interpolate for every year (1994, 1995, 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999, 2000)

Thanks

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] spatio-temporal areal level modelling
parts:
Hi,
Computing such predictions is limited by available computer memory.
Whether those predictions are _useful_ is a different questions, and the answer depends on the structure of the problem; slow trends may yield sensible predictions, whereas quickly varying random effects will show up as large posterior uncertainty in the predictions. The good news is that if you have enough memory to compute the predictions, then the posterior output will show if the predictions are useful for a specific purpose.

Finn
